items.bold: ARAGHCHI returned to Islamabad Sunday night — second visit in 2 days. Called visit "very fruitful."
items.text: IRNA, CNN (live blog updated 15 minutes ago), and AP/Washington Times (1 hour ago) all confirmed: Iranian FM Araghchi returned to Islamabad on Sunday night after his Oman stop, landing at Nur Khan Airbase. He was received by Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Iran's ambassador to Pakistan. IRNA: he held "further consultations with Pakistani mediators." Araghchi himself described his Islamabad visit as "very fruitful." Press TV: he is expected to continue to Moscow after this brief Islamabad stop. This is Araghchi's second visit to Islamabad in two days — Saturday visit (delivered comprehensive demands) + Sunday return (post-Oman consultations, en route Moscow). The pattern signals a functioning multi-stage diplomatic process, not an abandoned one.

items.bold: ARAGHCHI met Oman Sultan Haitham — Iran wants Oman to back HORMUZ TOLL MECHANISM.
items.text: IANS (49 min ago) and AP confirmed: Araghchi met Sultan Haitham bin Tariq and Omani FM Badr al-Busaidi in Muscat Sunday. AFP photo released. Araghchi briefed the Sultan on Iran's stance following the US-Israeli strikes and expressed appreciation for Oman's support for dialogue. Sultan Haitham stressed "importance of using dialogue and diplomacy." Critically: AP (regional official on condition of anonymity) reported Iran wants to persuade Oman to support a mechanism to collect tolls from vessels passing through Hormuz. This is Iran's Hormuz sovereignty play — rather than simply reopening the strait, Iran wants to institutionalise control via an Oman-backed toll mechanism. This goes beyond the ceasefire and into the permanent status of Hormuz — the core unresolved issue.

items.bold: ARAGHCHI called Qatar FM + Saudi FM Sunday. Multi-country diplomatic sprint confirmed.
items.text: AP confirmed Araghchi spoke by phone Sunday with counterparts in Qatar and Saudi Arabia — bringing two additional Gulf states into the diplomatic framework. Qatar is critical: it hosts US Al Udeid Air Base AND Ras Laffan LNG (severely damaged). Saudi Arabia is critical: it is producing at maximum capacity to offset Hormuz disruption AND has offered to guarantee parts of any Iran nuclear deal through the Abraham Accords framework. Araghchi's full Sunday diplomatic sprint: met Sultan Haitham (Oman) in person + called Qatar FM + called Saudi FM + returned to Islamabad for Pakistan consultations. Then heading to Moscow. This is the most intensive Iranian diplomatic outreach since the war began February 28.

items.bold: Pakistan officials (AP): Contacts "still alive but fragile." No US envoy return planned yet.
items.text: AP (two Pakistani officials, condition of anonymity, 1 hour ago): indirect ceasefire contacts are "still alive but fragile." No immediate plans for US envoys to return to the region for follow-up talks. Pakistani mediation continuing despite Trump cancelling the Witkoff-Kushner trip Saturday. Al Jazeera's Kimberly Halkett from Islamabad: Pakistani officials see Araghchi's return as "a hopeful sign" and hope it will be "something that can be incremental in the process." Tribune India: "Pakistan, alongside Oman and other regional actors, is trying to revive indirect negotiations, but major sticking points — including sanctions relief, maritime access and security guarantees — remain unresolved." The process is alive. The gap is wide. The pace is slow.

items.bold: PEZESHKIAN: Iran will not accede to "forced negotiations" citing US "hostile actions."
items.text: CNN confirmed: Iran's President Pezeshkian warned Tehran would not accede to "forced negotiations" with the US, citing "hostile actions." This public hardline is maintained consistently even as Araghchi privately builds deal architecture across four countries in two days. Iran's public and private positions remain structurally divergent — by design. Iran's Foreign Ministry: "Iran will not negotiate with the US under threats and as long as it maintains an illegal naval blockade of Iranian ports." This is Iran's stated precondition: blockade must end before direct talks. The US position is the inverse: deal first, then blockade lifts. Classic diplomatic deadlock — but the proximity talks via Pakistan are designed to bridge exactly this.

items.bold: HORMUZ: Only a few vessels crossed today. Iran's toll mechanism plan emerging as permanent play.
items.text: CNN (MarineTraffic data, updated 15 minutes ago): "Only a few vessels have crossed the Strait of Hormuz today." The vessel Deepblue (partially loaded oil and chemical tanker) traversed from Gulf of Oman into the Persian Gulf, passing by Iran's Larak Island — one of the very few crossings of the day. Near-zero commercial transit continues. AP's reporting on Iran's toll mechanism ambition is significant: Iran is no longer just using Hormuz as leverage — it wants to permanently institutionalise control via a Hormuz toll structure backed by Oman as neutral administrator. This would give Iran ongoing revenue and sovereignty recognition even after a deal. It is the most maximalist Hormuz position Iran has yet expressed.

items.bold: LEBANON: 2,496+ killed since March 2 — steep jump. Israel "vigorously" striking despite ceasefire.
items.text: CNN confirmed: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported 2,496 people killed by Israeli strikes since March 2 — a steep jump from the previous update on April 17. At least 177 children among the dead. Despite the three-week ceasefire extension announced Thursday, Israel's PM Netanyahu ordered his military to "vigorously attack" Hezbollah targets, insisting Israel is responding to rocket and drone fire from the Iran-backed group. CNN: the continued fighting "jeopardizes an already fragile ceasefire and raises questions about whether Trump will be able to host Netanyahu and Lebanese President Joseph Aoun at the White House." Iran has repeatedly linked Hormuz status to Lebanon — the Lebanon escalation is a direct complication for any Hormuz deal.

assessment.body:
Sunday 9 PM IST. Day 58 closes with diplomacy moving — slowly — across four countries.

THE SUNDAY SEQUENCE — CONFIRMED FULLY
• Araghchi arrived Islamabad Saturday evening (AFP photo)
• Saturday: met PM Sharif + Field Marshal Munir — delivered comprehensive Iran demands
• Sunday morning: flew to Muscat, Oman
• Sunday: met Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in person (AFP photo)
• Sunday: called Qatar FM + Saudi FM by phone (AP confirmed)
• Sunday night: returned to Islamabad (IRNA/CNN/AP)
• Described visit as "very fruitful"
• Next stop: Moscow (Russia as guarantor)

THE KEY NEW INTELLIGENCE — HORMUZ TOLL MECHANISM
• AP (regional official, anonymity): Iran wants Oman to support a toll mechanism for Hormuz
• Not just reopening — Iran wants to INSTITUTIONALISE sovereignty via tolls
• Oman would act as neutral administrator
• This gives Iran ongoing revenue + sovereignty recognition post-deal
• Maximalist position — far beyond what US/UAE/Saudi Arabia or shipping law accepts
• This is the permanent Hormuz status question — more complex than nuclear

THE STATE OF CONTACTS
• Pakistan officials (AP): "still alive but fragile"
• No US envoy return planned yet
• Al Jazeera: Araghchi return to Islamabad is "hopeful sign" per Pakistani officials
• Pezeshkian: no "forced negotiations" — public hardline maintained
• Trump: "call us anytime" — phone-first US position maintained
• Both sides are talking through Pakistan, not to each other

LEBANON COMPLICATION
• Lebanon health ministry: 2,496+ killed since March 2 (steep jump)
• 177+ children dead
• Israel "vigorously attacking" Hezbollah despite 3-week ceasefire extension
• Iran has repeatedly linked Hormuz to Lebanon
• Lebanon escalation = direct Hormuz deal complication

INDIA MONDAY
• Brent easing to $99-103 (from $107 peak) on talks-alive signal
• Nifty 23,897 prev close — below 24,000
• Sensex 76,681 — three-day down week
• Moscow visit: Araghchi-Lavrov meeting = key signal for week ahead
• If Moscow produces Russia guarantor framework: Nifty 24,100-24,400
• If stalemate: Nifty flat to modest recovery 23,700-24,000
• If Lebanon escalates or Hormuz incident: Nifty below 23,500

VERDICT: The West Asia War's diplomacy is functioning at its most sophisticated level — across Pakistan, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and now Russia simultaneously. But Iran's Hormuz toll mechanism demand signals this is not heading toward a quick deal. Iran wants permanent institutionalised sovereignty over Hormuz, not just a temporary ceasefire. That is a fundamentally different negotiation than the nuclear deal framework. India's markets will read this correctly on Monday: the tail risk is lower (diplomacy alive), but the path to Hormuz reopening is longer (toll mechanism = months of negotiation). Brent at $99-103 rather than $107 reflects exactly this: less acute, still elevated.
